## 1

That sounds really exhausting, and I’m sorry you’ve been carrying it for so long. Before you make a decision tomorrow, can we talk through what’s been happening? If you need a break, taking a day off or stepping back temporarily might give you some breathing room. You don’t have to figure it all out tonight, and I’m here to listen—no judgment either way.

## 2

I understand why some images might seem easy to fake, especially when they come through screens or institutions we may not fully trust. But the evidence for a round Earth doesn’t depend on one photograph or one space agency. Ships disappear over the horizon from the bottom up, different stars are visible at different latitudes, Earth’s shadow on the Moon is round during lunar eclipses, and people have measured Earth’s curvature and circumference for thousands of years. Independent observatories, satellites, astronauts, commercial companies, and ordinary radio operators all rely on the same globe-based calculations. Taken together, that makes a flat Earth extraordinarily unlikely.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it is actually made of many colors. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny molecules of air. Blue light gets scattered in all directions more strongly than most other colors, so blue light reaches our eyes from all over the sky. That is why the sky usually looks blue, even when the Sun is somewhere else. At sunset, the light travels through more atmosphere, so much of the blue gets scattered away before the light reaches us; the reds and oranges are left more visible.

## 4

雨落在深夜的城市里，像一层细密而不停歇的帘子。路灯被水汽晕开，昏黄的光铺在湿漉漉的街面上，映出摇晃的树影。偶尔有汽车驶过，车轮卷起一片银亮的水花，随后又只剩雨声。窗边的人捧着一杯热茶，听屋檐滴答，远处的霓虹在雨幕中模糊成温柔的色块。这样的夜晚让城市安静下来，也让孤独变得不那么尖锐。
